structures.name: Dual currency deposit / investment, gold-linked (DCD / DCI / "premium" account)
structures.one_liner: A short deposit with an embedded sold option: enhanced coupon, but principal repays in gold or cash, whichever is worse at the strike.
structures.how_it_works: The client places a deposit in a base choice (USD, AUD, EUR, SGD, MYR...) or in gold, picks an alternate choice and a strike (target conversion rate), and a tenor of typically 1 week to 3 months. Economically the client sells the bank a put option on the alternate choice with the same strike and expiry; the option premium is paid out as the "enhanced interest", so the all-in coupon is deposit rate + annualised premium. At the notification/fixing date the bank compares gold-per-base against the strike: if the alternate choice has weakened through the strike the bank exercises and repays principal plus interest converted into the alternate choice at the strike; otherwise it repays in the base choice. Interest normally accrues on an ACT/360 or 30/360 basis and is paid in whichever asset is delivered, so a gold-converted ticket pays interest in ounces.
structures.why_client_buys: It monetises a view the client already holds - either "I am happy to own gold 4-6% cheaper" or "I am happy to sell some of my gold at a level above spot" - and it pays a headline yield many multiples of a fixed deposit while the client waits.
structures.what_bank_earns: The bank buys the option from the client at a mark-down to its own volatility: the client is typically shown a coupon worth roughly 60-80% of the theoretical option premium, and the desk keeps the rest plus the bid/offer on the conversion at strike and on the metal leg. There is no explicit fee (Citi's own information sheet says "no explicit fees and charges"), which is exactly why the margin sits in the option price.
structures.typical_terms: Tenor 1 week to 3 months (Citi HK goes to 6 months); minimums USD10,000 (Citi HK), SGD30,000 (StanChart gold PCI), MYR40,000-50,000 (CIMB / HSBC Malaysia); strike set 1-5% out of the money for the short tenors; indicative annualised coupons typically mid-single-digit to low-teens depending on gold volatility and strike distance - Citi's own worked examples use 10.0% p.a. and 9.7% p.a. on a 1-month ticket, and CIMB advertises "potential double-digit returns p.a.". No early termination right for the client on most versions.
structures.client_risk: This is not a deposit: it is an unsecured claim on the bank plus a short option, so if gold falls through the strike the client is long gold bought at the strike and the coupon is only a partial buffer - Citi's sheet warns of a maximum loss of 100% of the investment amount. The client also gives up all upside beyond the coupon and cannot break the trade.

examples.product: Gold Premium Investment (GPI) - "Currency Linked Paper Gold Investment"

Worked examples: 50 oz gold, 1M, strike XAU/USD 1,500 at 10% p.a. (interest paid in 0.42 oz of gold); and a USD-base case at 9.7% p.a.

Every converted ticket creates a loco-London unallocated balance that the desk can then bid for as custody or roll into a deposit - the DCI book is a metal-liability feeder for the desk.

structures.name: Lombard / margin lending against precious metal
structures.one_liner: A revolving credit line secured by pledged bullion, metal accounts or metal ETFs - liquidity without selling the gold.
structures.how_it_works: The client pledges allocated bars in the bank's vault, an unallocated metal account, a metal exchange-traded fund or gold-linked notes; the bank assigns each position a lending value (market value x advance rate) and lends up to the aggregate lending value, usually as a multi-currency revolving facility or overdraft priced off SOFR/SONIA/SARON plus a spread. The collateral is marked daily; if exposure exceeds the lending value the client gets a margin call (top up cash/metal, repay, or reduce), and after a short cure period the bank can sell the metal or close the position itself under the pledge. Allocated bars in the bank's own vault get the best treatment because the bank has possession; third-party-vaulted or ETF collateral gets a haircut for transfer and liquidation risk.
structures.why_client_buys: Liquidity without a disposal: no capital-gains event, no loss of the gold position in a bull market, and the ability to fund a property deposit, a capital call or a tax bill while staying long metal. UHNW families also use it to arbitrage cheap collateralised funding against expected asset returns and to keep the gold inside a succession structure.
structures.what_bank_earns: Net interest margin on a fully secured loan (typically 75-200bp over the reference rate at PB level), plus the custody/storage fee on the pledged metal, plus the retained flow: the client keeps trading and hedging with the same bank, and the desk gets the liquidation right if it goes wrong. Capital cost is low because the collateral is liquid and daily-marked.
structures.typical_terms: Advance rates published by banks are rare; observed ranges are roughly 50-70% on physical bullion and unallocated metal at conventional lenders, up to 80% at the aggressive end (Emirates Money's DMCC-warranted gold loan advertised up to 80% LTV, minimum AED30,000, 6-36 months), 70-75% on major gold ETFs (Saxo gives 75% collateral value to Rating-1 stocks/ETFs), and materially less - often 0-50% - on single-issuer structured notes and gold-mining equities. Non-bank specialists quote 70-85% LTV at 5.5-9.9% interest for 6-24 months. Retail-regulated markets cap it: RBI caps Indian gold loans at 75% LTV.
structures.client_risk: It is a leveraged long gold position in the form of a loan: at 70% loan-to-value a 25-30% drawdown triggers a margin call, and collateral can be sold to meet it, which realises the position and the tax event the borrowing was arranged to defer. Cross-collateralisation clauses mean a shortfall elsewhere in the portfolio can draw on the metal, and with unallocated collateral the client ranks as an unsecured creditor of the bank.

A bullion desk that will commit a firm liquidation bid lets the credit committee raise the advance rate - that is the desk's direct revenue lever into the wealth book.

structures.name: Selling puts on gold to enhance yield (cash-secured puts / gold-linked notes)
structures.one_liner: Client is paid a premium today to commit to buying gold at a lower strike - the same trade as a DCI, in option or note form.
structures.how_it_works: The client sells a European put on gold against the dollar (or on GLD/IAU for a US-domiciled account) struck 3-10% below spot, with cash or a credit line set aside to fund delivery, and receives the premium up front. In private banking the trade is usually wrapped as a note sold at a discount to par - DBS Hong Kong's Gold-Linked Note is exactly this: the investor buys a note on paper gold at a discounted price and receives par in cash at maturity if gold fixes at or above strike, or takes delivery of the metal at strike if it fixes below. Adding an American up-and-out knock-out above spot turns it into a KO Gold-Linked Note: the note terminates early with the accrued yield if gold rallies through the barrier, which is how the desk pays a higher headline coupon.
structures.why_client_buys: The client wants gold but thinks it is extended: being paid 8-12% annualised to wait, and buying 4-5% below spot if assigned, beats a limit order. For an existing gold holder it is a way to size up on weakness at a known price.
structures.what_bank_earns: The option premium net of what it passes to the client (a 3-5 volatility point mark-down is typical at PB level), the hedging P&L on delta-hedging the short put back into the interbank market, and, on the note format, the funding benefit of holding the client's discounted principal for the tenor.
structures.typical_terms: Tenor 2 weeks to 3 months (1 month is the standard ticket); strike 3-10% below spot; notional 100 oz to several thousand oz - DBS quotes paper gold in a 100 oz minimum, and its worked example is 1,000 oz; indicative annualised yields 6-15% depending on volatility and strike, quoted on a 360-day basis. Assignment is cash-settled into an unallocated metal account rather than bars unless the client asks for allocation.
structures.client_risk: Unlimited-ish downside below the strike less premium: a 20% gold sell-off leaves the client owning metal 15%+ underwater with only the coupon as compensation, and the position is illiquid - most PB notes have no early termination right and the unwind price is the issuer's own mark. With a knock-out the client keeps the full downside but loses the upside scenarios that pay.

examples.product: Gold-Linked Note (GLN) and Knock-Out Gold-Linked Note (KO GLN) on Paper Gold
examples.detail: Product booklet: GLN is traded on a discounted-principal basis and is economically a short put; worked example 1,000 oz paper gold, 1-month, strike USD1,200 when market is USD1,250, agreed yield 8.00% p.a. (discount USD7,947 on a USD1.2m notional, annualised 360/30). Paper gold spot minimum 100 oz; structured notes on paper gold capped at 1-year tenor.

The desk also sets the strike grid the RMs quote from (spot minus 3/5/7/10% at 1w/1m/3m) and should publish an indicative yield board daily - that board is what makes the product sellable at scale.

structures.name: Covered calls on gold, and packaged gold covered-call funds
structures.one_liner: Client sells upside on metal they already own for premium income; the packaged version is a gold income fund with a call-writing overlay.
structures.how_it_works: Against an existing holding - allocated bars, an unallocated account or a gold ETF - the client sells a call struck above spot and keeps the premium. If gold fixes above the strike the metal is called away at the strike (or cash-settled against the account), so the client has converted uncapped upside into a defined coupon. The packaged version does the same systematically inside a fund: hold gold ETFs (or gold-producer equities), write short-dated calls on a portion of the book, and distribute the premium monthly. Some funds use a synthetic version - long call options on GLD instead of GLD itself, with short calls written against them - which changes the risk profile materially.
structures.why_client_buys: Income from a non-yielding asset. Gold pays nothing, so a client sitting on a large, long-held bullion position - often for succession or crisis-hedge reasons - can turn it into a 6-12% distributing asset while keeping the exposure.
structures.what_bank_earns: On bilateral calls: the option mark-down plus hedging P&L, exactly as on the put side. On the fund: management fee (0.7-1.5% is typical for covered-call vehicles), sub-management fee split, plus the execution and custody of the underlying ETFs. The fund format is strategically better for the bank - it converts an episodic RM trade into recurring AUM.
structures.typical_terms: Bilateral: 1-3 month tenor, strike 3-8% above spot, premium 1-3% of notional for a 1-month at 5% out of the money in normal volatility - annualising to roughly 8-20% depending on the volatility regime. Funds: monthly distributions, headline yields around 8-11% in the 2026 gold volatility environment, MER 0.7-1.0%, partial overwriting (typically 25-50% of the book) to preserve some upside.
structures.client_risk: If gold rallies through the strike the metal is called away and the position participates only up to that level, which is what holders noticed in 2025-26 when gold moved several hundred dollars in a matter of weeks. The premium cushions a limited amount of downside. On packaged funds, part of the distribution can be return of capital, so the headline yield and the economic return are not the same number.

structures.desk_hook: The desk supplies the call volatility and, critically, the delivery mechanics: if the metal is allocated, someone has to be able to deliver bars or unallocated against assignment. For the fund format the desk can be the options counterparty or the FX/metal hedge provider on the currency-hedged share classes (which is where the 30bp-a-year hedged-share-class cost sits - see our ETF calculations work).

structures.name: Gold accumulators and decumulators (AQ / DQ)
structures.one_liner: A strip of forwards: the client buys gold daily at a fixed discount until a knock-out - and buys double if the price falls below the strike.
structures.how_it_works: An accumulator is a series of daily (or weekly) forward purchases of a fixed quantity of metal at a strike set at a discount to spot - historically 10-20% for equities, tighter (typically 2-6%) for gold because metal volatility is lower. Two features define the payoff: an up-and-out knock-out, so the contract terminates as soon as spot closes above a barrier a few percent over the initial fixing (capping the client's profit at a few days or weeks of accrued discount); and a gearing/multiplier, so on any fixing below the strike the client must take two (sometimes four) times the daily quantity. A decumulator mirrors it: the client sells metal daily at a premium, with the doubling obligation on the upside - which is the version that has no natural cap on loss. Tenor is usually 3-12 months and the client posts margin, often around 40% of the full notional, against mark-to-market.
structures.why_client_buys: In Hong Kong and Singapore these are the staple flow product for entrepreneurs who are already comfortable with leverage: the client is told they are "buying gold at a discount every day", the RM shows a scenario grid in which the discount compounds, and the product is bookable in size against an existing Lombard line. Decumulators sell to family offices monetising a large legacy bullion position at above spot.
structures.what_bank_earns: A large embedded structuring margin - the client is effectively short a strip of options and the bank buys that volatility cheap - plus margin-financing interest on the notional and the bid/offer on every daily fixing. Accumulators are among the highest-margin flow products in Asian private banking, which is precisely why regulators watch them.
structures.typical_terms: Tenor 3-12 months, daily fixings, strike 2-6% below spot for gold, knock-out 2-5% above initial spot, 2x gearing below strike, margin c.40% of notional, minimum notionals typically USD1m+ and professional-investor only. Decumulator terms mirror this.
structures.client_risk: The payoff is asymmetric: the upside knocks out after a modest gain while the downside continues at a doubled quantity for the full tenor. Hong Kong Monetary Authority guidance notes that accumulator investors can be exposed up to the full notional, and that for decumulators the exposure is open-ended if the underlying rallies. In a fast sell-off the client keeps accumulating twice the daily quantity, and any Lombard line behind it faces margin calls at the same time.

examples.product: Guidance on Selling of Accumulators (14 March 2025; predecessor circulars 2010 and 2014)
examples.detail: Requires sales essentially to Professional Investors, highest risk rating, suitability and concentration assessment on full notional (with a flexible FX-only threshold framework of 2% for USDHKD, 40% for other major pairs, 100% otherwise), and prominent disclosure of knock-out clauses, multipliers/loss magnification, tenor and margin risk. The HKMA has confirmed 'accumulator' covers decumulators and similarly-structured products whatever they are called.

examples.firm: Asian private banks generally (HSBC GPB Asia, Standard Chartered PB, UBS, JPM PB, DBS PB)
examples.product: OTC accumulators / decumulators on XAU
examples.detail: Trade press confirms AQDQ remained one of the two most popular flow products in Asian private wealth through 2026 and that investors used AQDQ specifically to accumulate gold exposure at predetermined levels during the 2026 rally. Bank-published documentation exists for equity and FX AQ/DQ (e.g. DBS HK product booklets) but the gold version is documented only in bespoke term sheets.

examples.product: OTC Accumulator & Decumulator product booklets (equity; FX incl. target and pivot-target variants)

The paper gold booklet stops at options, forwards and (KO) gold-linked notes, confirming that gold AQ/DQ sits on the bespoke/PB shelf rather than the published retail shelf.

structures.desk_hook: The desk prices and hedges the strip - a long stream of short puts with a barrier, so it needs a barrier-capable gold volatility book and daily fixing capacity - and supplies the daily fixings, the metal delivery into the client's unallocated account, and the risk transfer to the interbank market. If the wealth business wants gold AQ/DQ, the desk has to be able to warehouse skew and barrier risk; that is the gating capability.
structures.in_our_catalogue: partly - we have 'OTC gold options / accumulators-decumulators' listed for HSBC GPB Asia and Standard Chartered PB in the otc_derivative bucket, both at knowledge confidence. No terms, no notionals, no other banks.

structures.name: Gold-linked structured notes
structures.one_liner: Bank debt whose redemption is a gold payoff - capital-protected, income, or leveraged - sold as the PB's core wrapper for a gold view.
structures.how_it_works: The issuer takes the client's principal, keeps a zero-coupon bond's worth to repay whatever capital is protected, and spends the rest on an option package on gold or a gold ETF; the note's terms are the option package. Notes are issued off an EMTN programme or as a structured deposit, with an issuer credit risk the client cannot diversify. In Asia the same economics appear as structured deposits (onshore China, Turkey) for regulatory reasons. Almost all PB notes are illiquid: the issuer quotes a bid, there is no exchange, and early exit costs 1-5 points.

sub_families.name: Capital-protected participation note
sub_families.mechanics: Zero-coupon bond plus a long call on XAU; client gets 100% of principal back plus a participation rate (typically 40-80%) in gold's rise, often with a cap.
sub_families.when_sold: To conservative or first-time gold buyers, and whenever rates are high enough to make the zero cheap - the standard 'I want gold but cannot lose money' answer.

sub_families.name: Reverse convertible / fixed coupon note (FCN)
sub_families.mechanics: Bond plus a sold put: high fixed coupon, principal repaid in cash unless gold is below the strike at maturity, in which case the client takes metal (or cash-settled loss) at the strike.
sub_families.when_sold: To yield-hungry clients with a neutral-to-mildly-bullish view; the highest-volume yield product in Asian PB alongside AQ/DQ.

sub_families.name: Autocallable
sub_families.mechanics: Periodic observation dates; if gold is above the initial level (or a declining trigger) the note redeems early with the accrued coupon, otherwise it continues; usually with a downside barrier that turns into a short put at maturity.
sub_families.when_sold: In range-bound or mildly rising markets, to recycle the same client money repeatedly - each autocall is a new ticket for the desk.

sub_families.name: Shark-fin
sub_families.mechanics: Capital protection plus an up-and-out call: the client participates in the rally up to a barrier, but if gold ever trades through the barrier the note knocks out and pays a small rebate coupon.
sub_families.when_sold: To clients who want protection and think gold grinds rather than spikes; popular as a short-tenor structured deposit in HK/China/Thailand.

sub_families.name: Twin-win
sub_families.mechanics: Capital protection with a down-and-out put plus a call: the client makes money on gold moving either way within a range, but a barrier breach on the downside converts the position into long gold from the strike.
sub_families.when_sold: Sold on high implied vol when the client has no directional view but expects a big move - classic around Fed and geopolitical events.

sub_families.name: Range accrual
sub_families.mechanics: Coupon accrues for each day gold fixes inside a defined range (e.g. 4,800-5,600); days outside accrue nothing; usually capital protected or lightly geared.
sub_families.when_sold: In quiet, high-carry markets to clients who want a rate-like coupon and believe in a stable band - it sells poorly in a trending gold market like 2025-26.

structures.why_client_buys: One ticket gives a precisely shaped payoff the client cannot build themselves, in a format their booking centre, custodian and reporting already handle, often with capital protection that makes a volatile asset board-approvable for a family office or a corporate treasury.
structures.what_bank_earns: The structuring margin embedded in the option package (typically 0.5-2.0% of notional for a 1-2 year note, higher on exotics), the funding benefit of issuing its own paper at a level cheaper than wholesale, distribution/retrocession fees if third-party issued, and the secondary bid/offer on every unwind.
structures.typical_terms: Tenors 6 months to 3 years (shark-fin and structured deposits often 3-12 months); minimums USD100k-250k at PB level, USD10k-50k for the retail structured-deposit versions; issuer is the bank or a G-SIB dealer; underlying is gold against the dollar spot fix or a gold ETF (GLD/IAU) for US-facing paper. Notes on gold have been issued in volume in 2026 - e.g. auto-callable notes linked to SPDR Gold Shares priced in June 2026 with annual call observations to 2029.
structures.client_risk: Issuer credit risk plus gap risk at the barrier plus illiquidity: the client's exit is the issuer's own mark, protection is only at maturity, and in the high-coupon formats (RC/FCN/autocall) the client is short a put that pays out exactly when gold falls hard and everything else in the portfolio is also falling.

The desk should also quote the secondary bid - a wealth business cannot scale a note shelf without a reliable unwind price.

structures.name: Gold leasing / metal deposits that pay a yield in metal
structures.one_liner: The client lends physical or unallocated gold to the bank for a term and is paid interest in grams or cash - a metal-denominated deposit.
structures.how_it_works: The client transfers title (or grants use) of metal to the bank for a fixed term; the bank becomes a debtor in ounces and pays a deposit rate. The bank funds itself in metal: it can on-lend to a refiner, miner or fabricator who needs metal working capital, use the metal in its own consignment/leasing book, or swap it for dollars (sell spot, buy forward) and capture the difference between the dollar rate it earns and the lease rate it pays. That is where the yield genuinely comes from - the gold lease rate is classically defined as the dollar rate minus the gold forward rate (LIBOR - GOFO), so a metal deposit is really a collateralised dollar deposit expressed in ounces. Interest is paid in metal (extra grams) or in currency, and the client gets back different bars from the ones deposited - the key disclosure point.
structures.why_client_buys: It turns a zero-yielding hoard into a yielding one without selling: a client holding 50kg for succession reasons can earn 0.5-4% p.a. in metal, which in a rising gold market compounds in the asset they actually want to own. In Turkey it also mobilises 'under-the-pillow' gold into the banking system with a state-supported incentive.
structures.what_bank_earns: The spread between what the bank can do with the metal (lease it out at the market lease rate, or swap it into dollars) and the deposit rate it pays the client - typically 50-200bp in normal conditions and far more in a squeeze - plus it gains a stable metal funding base that supports the desk's consignment and financing book.
structures.typical_terms: Tenors 1, 3, 6 and 12 months are the market convention; minimums from 50-100g (Turkish participation banks) to 1kg+ or 100oz+ for bank-level deposits; rates track the lease-rate curve - historical gold deposit rate averages were c.1.4% (1989-99), 0.54% (2000-09) and 0.24% (2010-19), with spikes (2.77% in October 2008) and again during the 2025-26 tightness. Retail 'gold grows gold' products quote a fixed grams-uplift instead (e.g. 2% for 12 months).
structures.client_risk: The client is an unsecured creditor in ounces: if the bank fails, the claim ranks with other creditors and the specific bars are gone (the metal is fungible and has been used). There is no deposit insurance on metal in most jurisdictions, early break is usually penal, and any bar-return obligation is 'same weight and fineness', not 'same bars'.

examples.product: 金生利 ("gold grows gold") gold deposit
examples.detail: Client buys a standard gold bar at the standard price and at maturity receives the bar plus extra grams as the return - e.g. a 50g bar on a 1-year term returning 2%, so 51g at maturity; larger tickets earn more (30 x 500g bars returning 30 x 10g). Economically a metal deposit paying interest in metal. CMB separately runs a 黄金账户 gold account with a 'store gold to generate gold' function.

examples.product: Altına Altın Katılma Hesabı (Gold-to-Gold Participation Account)
examples.detail: Every gram deposited is deployed into the real sector and the profit is returned to the client as gold. Minimum 100g for a 1-month maturity, 50g for 3-month to 1-year maturities; partial withdrawals allowed above the minimum balance without breaking the term. Shariah-compliant profit-share rather than interest.

examples.product: Fiziki Altın Katılma Hesabı - FATSİ (Physical Gold Participation Account)
examples.detail: Physical gold delivered via branch, 'Golden Days' collection events or contracted jewellers; no minimum; 3, 6 or 12-month terms; additional return of 2% / 3% / 4% by tenor paid up front by the central bank in TRY, with exchange-rate difference and profit share also paid in TRY; profit-sharing ratio 95-5. This is the Turkish gold-mobilisation scheme, not a pure commercial lease.

examples.firm: Turkish conventional banks (İşbank, Yapı Kredi, Garanti BBVA, QNB Türkiye, Ziraat, DenizBank)
examples.product: Vadeli Altın Hesabı (term gold deposit)
examples.detail: Term deposits denominated in grams of gold paying a gold interest rate, with minimums from a few hundred grams to 1kg. Already in our catalogue, mostly at knowledge confidence.

examples.product: Gold deposit rates - a guidance paper
examples.detail: The reference text for the mechanics: central bank places allocated gold on deposit with a bullion bank, gold is returned with interest paid in gold or currency but with different bars; most common maturities 1M/3M/12M; lease rate derived as LIBOR - GOFO; historical average deposit rates 1.4% (1989-99), 0.54% (2000-09), 0.24% (2010-19), peak 2.77% (Oct 2008).

structures.desk_hook: This IS the desk's product: the wealth business is the origination channel for metal liabilities that the desk on-lends to industrial borrowers or swaps into dollars. The desk sets the client deposit rate off its own lease-rate curve, manages the borrower side (refiners, jewellers, catalyst users), and owns the credit decision on who the metal goes to. Note the reverse position too: our desk-focus work prioritises the client BORROWING against metal (PM margin loan), which is the mirror of this trade.
structures.in_our_catalogue: partly - CMB, Kuveyt Türk and the Turkish term-gold accounts are in as gold_deposit_dci; the Depo/Lease matrix in DEEP_DIVES covers the corporate/bank side (279 clients with existing leasing/consignment). The private-client metal-deposit product line is thin outside China and Turkey.

structures.name: Client gold forwards and prepaid forwards
structures.one_liner: Buying or selling metal for a future date - or getting cash today against metal delivered later - without an option in sight.
structures.how_it_works: A forward locks a price for delivery in 1-12 months; the forward price is spot plus the dollar rate minus the lease rate, so in a normal market the client pays a small premium to defer, and in a squeeze (backwardation, as in parts of 2025-26) the deferral can be free or better. A prepaid forward reverses the cash flow: the client sells metal forward and takes most of the cash today, with the bank holding the metal or the delivery obligation - economically a secured loan repaid in metal, often more tax- and balance-sheet-friendly than a Lombard loan. Private banks offer forwards on a margined basis (e.g. DBS HK: buy/sell paper gold forward, covered or margined, up to 1-year tenor) so the client can defer payment while fixing the price.
structures.why_client_buys: To fix the price of a planned purchase or sale (a family buying 100kg over a year, a jeweller-owner monetising inventory), to defer settlement past a tax or reporting date, or to raise cash against metal without a credit line - the prepaid forward is the private-client version of a producer's prepay.
structures.what_bank_earns: Forward points spread (the desk quotes the lease rate wide on both sides), the funding margin on any prepay, and margin interest on leveraged forward positions. Prepaid forwards also lock up metal the desk can lease out for the term.
structures.typical_terms: Tenors 1-12 months standard (longer needs exceptional approval at most banks); minimum 100 oz gold / 10,000 oz silver at DBS-type shelves; margined forwards require 5-20% initial margin with daily marks; prepaid forwards typically advance 70-90% of spot value.
structures.client_risk: Full linear price risk with leverage: a margined forward gets margin-called like any leveraged position and the bank can close it out. On a prepaid forward the client has irreversibly sold upside above the forward price and carries the bank's performance risk on the metal return.

examples.product: Forward transactions on Paper Gold and Silver (covered and margined)
examples.detail: Product booklet permits buying forward on a covered basis and buying/selling forward on a margined basis with tenor up to 1 year (longer requires exceptional approval); close-out requires an offsetting contract by 5pm HK time on the third trading day before settlement, failing which the bank offsets at the client's cost. Minimum spot/forward size 100 oz gold, 10,000 oz silver; no physical settlement.

examples.firm: Bank Julius Baer, Pictet Wealth Management, LGT, Bank of China (HK), Hang Seng
examples.product: Precious-metals spot/forward/option and margin trading for private clients
examples.detail: All run a client PM trading desk covering spot, forwards and leveraged positions (Hang Seng 'Gold Master' FX & precious-metal margin trading; BOCHK precious metals and FX margin). Already in our otc_derivative records.

structures.desk_hook: Forward points, lease-rate curve, margin methodology and the loco-London delivery leg. The desk's forward curve is the raw material for every other structure on this list - DCI strikes, note zeros and accumulator strips all price off it.
structures.in_our_catalogue: partly - the otc_derivative bucket (13-16 records) covers PM spot/forward/margin trading at Julius Baer, Pictet, LGT, BOCHK, Hang Seng, Swissquote, Phillip; prepaid forwards for private clients are absent.

structures.name: Physical gold repo / sale-and-repurchase for wealthy clients
structures.one_liner: The client sells metal to the bank and agrees to buy it back at a fixed forward price - financing that never touches the credit file as a loan.
structures.how_it_works: Title in the bars passes to the bank against cash at (or slightly below) spot; simultaneously the client agrees to repurchase the same weight and fineness at a forward date and price. The repurchase price minus the sale price is the financing cost, expressed as a repo rate; the haircut (sale price versus market) is the bank's margin protection and is re-marked periodically like a securities repo. Because the bank owns the metal outright for the term, it can lease it, use it to square a short or deliver it into its own clearing obligations - which is why a repo is usually cheaper for the client than a Lombard loan against the same bars. Variable-margin versions add daily marks and margin transfers, just like GMRA.
structures.why_client_buys: Cheaper financing than a secured loan, no revaluation of a credit line, and it works for clients whose metal sits outside a bankable portfolio (a family vault, a DMCC warrant, a refinery receipt). It is also the standard route for corporates and family offices that hold metal as inventory rather than investment.
structures.what_bank_earns: The repo rate over its own funding cost, plus the use of the metal for the term (lease income or avoided borrowing cost), plus the haircut buffer. For a bullion desk, client repo is the cheapest metal borrowing available.
structures.typical_terms: Tenors overnight to 12 months (3-6 months typical); haircuts 5-20% depending on bar form and location; documentation under a bespoke sale-and-repurchase agreement or GMRA-style terms; metal must be LBMA Good Delivery or refinery-warranted for the best pricing.
structures.client_risk: Legal title passes on the first leg, so between the two dates the client holds a contractual claim rather than ownership of the metal, and ranks as an unsecured creditor of the bank. Mark-to-market calls can require cash top-ups, and if the repurchase does not take place the client's economics are settled at the repo price.

examples.product: Precious Metals REPO alongside gold loans and leasing
examples.detail: Named in the bank's own 2025 bullion-service materials as part of the gold-backed financing suite for clients using vaulted metal and certificates as collateral; already captured in our catalogue (verified) under lombard_vs_metal.

examples.firm: Bullion banks / ICBC Standard, and our own book
examples.product: Metal and commodity repo with corporates and holders
examples.detail: Our repo.json work has already identified 159 names that have transacted repo (31 metal-specific). The private-client version is the same instrument with a smaller ticket and a family-office counterparty.

structures.desk_hook: Directly the desk's balance sheet: the desk provides the cash, takes the metal, sets the haircut and lends the metal on. This is the highest-margin way for a bullion desk to monetise a wealth relationship, and it is the private-client analogue of the doré registered-pledge and refining-catalyst REPO deal shapes already on our live structure list.
structures.in_our_catalogue: partly - Emirates NBD's PM repo is there; the DEEP_DIVES 'Repo'/'Proven repo' tabs cover corporates. No private bank other than ENBD is recorded as offering client gold repo.

structures.name: Precious-metal options and collars for private clients
structures.one_liner: Bespoke puts, calls, zero-cost collars and leveraged forwards on gold booked directly with the client, not wrapped in a note.
structures.how_it_works: The PB desk quotes the client vanilla gold against the dollar options (or gold against EUR, CHF, JPY, AUD), risk reversals and zero-cost collars - buy a protective put, sell a call to pay for it - as well as leveraged forwards (target redemption, pivot) for clients who want a better-than-forward rate in exchange for gearing. Options are booked bilaterally under an ISDA or the bank's own derivatives terms, margined against the Lombard line, and can be unwound before expiry at the desk's price. For a client with a very large physical position, a collar is the cleanest way to protect a concentrated holding without selling it and without a tax event.
structures.why_client_buys: Protection or precision: a family that holds 500kg through a bull run can floor the value into a liquidity event; a client who is about to receive metal (an inheritance, a refinery payout, a mining dividend in kind) can hedge the interim. Zero-cost collars are attractive because there is no cash outlay.
structures.what_bank_earns: Vol spread on both legs of the collar (the desk is typically 2-4 vols wide to private clients versus interbank), plus margin financing and the unwind spread. Concentrated-position hedging is also defensive revenue: it keeps the asset on the platform instead of being sold.
structures.typical_terms: Tenors 1-12 months most commonly; minimum notionals roughly USD250k-1m equivalent (2,000-20,000 oz is institutional; private clients trade 100-5,000 oz); collar strikes commonly -10% put / +12-15% call for 6-12 months depending on skew; margin required against the short leg.
structures.client_risk: Short option legs can be margin-called, and a collar caps participation on an asset the client may be holding for protection. Leveraged forwards such as target-redemption structures and pivots behave differently from a plain forward: they knock out in the client's favourable scenario and gear up in the unfavourable one, in the same way an accumulator does.

examples.product: Leveraged precious-metals trading and OTC derivatives (24-hour FX & precious metals desk)
examples.detail: Published PB capability covering spot, forward and options in gold, silver, platinum and palladium, leveraged - a representative example of the PM option shelf inside a pure-play private bank.

examples.product: Hedging and OTC derivatives on specific positions (Capital Markets)
examples.detail: Citi PB markets a position-hedging service including precious metals - the collar-on-a-concentrated-holding use case; in our catalogue as verified.

examples.product: Gold Master - FX and precious-metal margin trading (XAU with leverage)
examples.detail: Retail-affluent leveraged XAU trading platform; the mass-market end of the same capability.

structures.desk_hook: gold against the dollar and gold-cross volatility surfaces, skew, and a quoting service the RMs can hit in size; plus margin and collateral integration with the Lombard book. The desk should publish a daily indicative collar grid - it is the easiest cross-sell into any client holding physical.
structures.in_our_catalogue: partly - otc_derivative records capture the trading capability at Julius Baer, Pictet, LGT, Citi, BOCHK, Hang Seng, Swissquote; specific option structures (collars, TARFs) are not broken out.

structures.name: Gold notes, funds and ETFs as Lombard collateral (the leverage loop)
structures.one_liner: The bank lends against the structured product it just sold, so the client buys more of it - the quiet engine of PB structured-product volume.
structures.how_it_works: Once a client owns a gold-linked note, fund or ETF, it enters the Lombard collateral schedule with its own advance rate: liquid physical gold ETFs typically get a high lending value (Saxo publishes 75% for Rating-1 ETFs), capital-protected notes issued by the lending bank itself get a moderate one because the payoff floor is known, and leveraged or barrier notes get little or none. The client then borrows against the position and reinvests, which is how a 5% note coupon becomes a 9% levered coupon on the pitch page. Self-issued paper creates a wrong-way problem - the collateral and the borrower's credit exposure are the same bank - so banks usually haircut their own notes harder or exclude them.
structures.why_client_buys: Levered carry: borrow at SOFR+1.5% against a note paying 8%, and the return on equity looks compelling as long as nothing gaps.
structures.what_bank_earns: Twice: the structuring margin on the note and the net interest margin on the loan, on the same client money - plus a bigger note ticket than the client could otherwise fund.
structures.typical_terms: Advance rates of roughly 70-75% for major physical gold ETFs, 40-70% for capital-protected notes, 0-40% for reverse convertibles/autocallables, 0% for anything with a knock-in already breached; all revisable at the bank's discretion at any time.
structures.client_risk: Compounding: when gold falls, the note's mark falls faster than spot (short-put gamma), the lending value is cut at the same moment, and the margin call lands while the client cannot exit the note except at the issuer's bid. This is the classic path from 'conservative income product' to forced liquidation.

examples.product: Lombard lending including against ETFs and structured notes
examples.detail: In our catalogue as offering Lombard lending against ETFs/structured notes with gold collateral - the standard Asian PB configuration.

examples.product: Published collateral-value schedule for ETFs
examples.detail: 75% collateral value for Rating 1 stock/ETF positions, with the right to reduce it for large or high-risk positions - the disclosed version of what PBs do privately with gold ETFs.

structures.desk_hook: Nothing directly, but the desk should care: leverage on gold notes is what converts a modest wealth allocation into large delta and vega that the desk has to warehouse, and it is the transmission mechanism for forced selling in a gold drawdown.
structures.in_our_catalogue: no - our lombard_vs_metal records do not distinguish collateral type, and no lending values are recorded.

structures.name: Shariah-compliant gold products (bai' as-sarf, murabahah, wakalah, participation accounts)
structures.one_liner: Gold products rebuilt to satisfy AAOIFI Standard 57: immediate delivery and possession, no interest, profit-share instead of coupon.
structures.how_it_works: Gold is a ribawi commodity, so a compliant trade must be spot with constructive possession on both legs (bai' as-sarf); deferred settlement, margin and most conventional options are out. The compliant shelf therefore looks like: (a) gold investment accounts backed 100% by allocated metal under wakalah (the bank is the client's agent) or murabahah (cost-plus sale with immediate title transfer); (b) gold instalment purchase - murabahah where the client takes title now and pays over time; (c) participation/profit-share gold deposits, where the metal is deployed in the real economy and the return is a share of actual profit, paid in gold; (d) Shariah dual-currency-style structures built from wa'd (unilateral promise) and murabahah legs rather than options. AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 57 on Gold (issued 2016 with the World Gold Council) is the reference text and unlocked most of this product set.
structures.why_client_buys: It is the only way a Shariah-observant client can hold and monetise gold in a bank; in Malaysia, Indonesia, Turkey and the Gulf this is a mass market, not a niche, and in Turkey it is also the main channel for mobilising physical hoards.
structures.what_bank_earns: Spread on the sale legs (the murabahah mark-up), the profit-share ratio on participation accounts (Kuveyt Türk discloses 95-5 in the client's favour on FATSİ), storage/agency fees, and the same underlying deployment economics as a conventional metal deposit.
structures.typical_terms: Entry points are deliberately tiny in retail-Islamic markets - MIGA-i starts at RM10 - while participation deposits run 1-12 months at 50-100g minimums; returns are quoted as profit-share ratios or expected rates rather than interest.
structures.client_risk: Same market risk as any gold holding, plus documentation risk (whether the client truly has title to allocated metal or merely a contractual claim) and the fact that profit-share returns are not guaranteed. Compliance opinions differ by jurisdiction - a structure approved in Malaysia may not pass in the Gulf.

examples.firm: AAOIFI with the World Gold Council
examples.product: Shari'ah Standard No. 57 on Gold and its Trading Controls (2016)
examples.detail: First standard setting rules for investing and dealing in gold; endorsed by AAOIFI's 20-scholar Shari'ah board; credited with catalysing gold investment accounts, physical gold ETFs, spot contracts and gold savings plans in Islamic finance.

examples.product: Maybank Islamic Gold Account-i (MIGA-i)
examples.detail: Shariah-compliant gold investment account: 999.9 purity, real-time online trading, physical redemption as bars, every transaction backed by physical metal with immediate ownership transfer and custody by an appointed agent; minimum initial purchase RM10 (RM50 for sole proprietors).

examples.product: Bank Islam Gold Account (BIGA-i)
examples.detail: 100% backed by physical gold, structured under wakalah with the bank acting as the client's agent (wakil).

examples.product: Gold-to-Gold and Physical Gold (FATSİ) participation accounts
examples.detail: See the leasing structure above - these are the Islamic metal-deposit format, paying profit share in gold (gold-to-gold) or in TRY with a central-bank-funded uplift of 2/3/4% by tenor (FATSİ).

structures.desk_hook: Physical supply into compliant allocated accounts (kilobars, 995/9999 to local standards), same-day delivery-versus-payment so possession is real, and a compliant financing structure (murabahah/tawarruq on metal) if the wealth business wants a Shariah Lombard equivalent. Note that the desk's conventional lease/repo mechanics generally do NOT translate - a compliant metal financing has to be built from sale contracts, not loans.
structures.in_our_catalogue: partly - Kuveyt Türk is in; the Malaysian and Indonesian Islamic gold accounts (MIGA-i, BIGA-i, Pegadaian/BSI) appear in the private-wealth sweep but are not tagged as a Shariah family, so the desk cannot see the segment.

structures.name: Gold accumulation / savings plans (GAP) - and why they are NOT accumulators
structures.one_liner: A regular-savings drip into unallocated gold, with optional conversion to bars - simple, huge in volume, and often confused with AQ/DQ.
structures.how_it_works: The client commits a fixed cash amount per month (or per day, in the Japanese and Chinese formats); the bank buys the equivalent weight of unallocated gold at its own price, accrues the grams in a metal passbook account, and allows conversion to physical bars or coins above a threshold weight, usually for a fabrication fee. There is no option, no leverage and no knock-out. The bank's margin is the bid/offer on each purchase (CMB, for example, widened its spot gold account spread from RMB2.4 to RMB3.0 per gram in February 2026) plus any storage or conversion fee.
structures.why_client_buys: Discipline and access: dollar-cost averaging into gold with no minimum lot and no storage problem. In China, Japan, Malaysia, Indonesia and Turkey these plans are the single largest private-client gold channel by account count.
structures.what_bank_earns: Pure spread and fee income on a sticky, recurring, near-zero-credit-risk balance - and the aggregate unallocated position is a stable metal funding base for the desk.
structures.typical_terms: Minimums from RM10 / RMB100 / JPY1,000 per month; spreads of roughly 0.3-1.0% per side; physical conversion at 10g/50g/100g/1kg denominations plus a fabrication fee; no maturity.
structures.client_risk: Unallocated means unsecured: the client is a creditor of the bank for the grams. The spread is the real cost and compounds with frequent purchases, and the conversion fee can be several percent on small bars.

examples.firm: China Merchants Bank, ICBC (积存金) and Chinese peers
examples.product: Gold accumulation plan / 黄金账户
examples.detail: Regular or lump-sum accumulation of unallocated gold with physical conversion; CMB's gold account combines purchase, regular investment, redemption and exchange, and includes the 'store gold to generate gold' deposit feature. CMB widened its gold account spread to RMB3.0/g in February 2026.

examples.firm: Maybank Islamic, Bank Islam (Malaysia); Pegadaian, BSI (Indonesia)
examples.product: Gold investment accounts / cicil emas instalment gold
examples.detail: The same savings mechanic in Shariah form, with instalment purchase of physical gold in Indonesia. Already partly in the catalogue as gold_savings_plan (32 records).

structures.desk_hook: Aggregated client accumulation flow is a daily physical/unallocated hedging requirement and a stable metal liability the desk can fund from - this is the flow a bullion desk wants to win when it pitches a wealth business, even though the product itself looks unglamorous.
structures.in_our_catalogue: yes - 32 gold_savings_plan plus 90-94 gold_account_unallocated and 26 gold_account_allocated records. This is the part of the 564 that is well covered; the terminology risk is that our taxonomy does not separate a savings plan from an accumulator derivative.

structures.name: Private participation in streaming, royalty and refinery/producer financings
structures.one_liner: Club-deal access for UHNW and family offices to metal-linked private credit: streams, royalties, prepays and refinery working capital.
structures.how_it_works: The bank syndicates a slice of a metal-linked private transaction to a small group of qualifying clients, usually through a feeder fund, a note issued off the bank's platform, or a direct participation. The underlying is a gold or silver stream (upfront cash for the right to buy future production at a fixed low price), a net smelter royalty, a producer prepay, or secured working capital to a refiner or trader. Returns come as contracted metal deliveries or fixed coupons secured on inventory and receivables, usually in the high single to low double digits, with tenors of 3-10 years and very limited liquidity.
structures.why_client_buys: Yield with a hard-asset link and optionality on the metal price, uncorrelated with the client's listed book, and the status of a deal that is not on anyone's platform. Families with mining-sector origins are natural buyers.
structures.what_bank_earns: Arrangement and syndication fees on the underlying deal, placement and management fees on the feeder, and the relationship benefit of showing UHNW clients institutional deal flow. It also lets the bank distribute risk it does not want to hold.
structures.typical_terms: Minimum tickets USD1-5m; 3-10 year lock-ups; target IRRs 8-15%; a feeder-fund or note wrapper with annual or semi-annual distributions; professional/accredited investors only.
structures.client_risk: Single-asset, single-jurisdiction operating risk (a stream is only worth what the mine produces), deep illiquidity, and a valuation the client cannot independently verify. These are the structures where a gold-price rally does not save a bad orebody.

examples.product: c.US$300m margin loan on Triple Flag shares plus an equity forward
examples.detail: The reverse case that is already our priority product: a holder of streaming-company equity borrows against it. It is the clearest evidence that PM-linked private positions are financeable at scale in the private/institutional market.

examples.firm: Private banks generally (UBS, JPM PB, Citi PB) via private-markets platforms
examples.product: Feeder access to metals-linked private credit and royalty funds
examples.detail: Standard private-markets shelf offering; not gold-specific on published pages, which is why our sweep did not capture it.

structures.desk_hook: The desk supplies the hedge (forward sales or options fixing the metal price on the stream/prepay), the offtake and physical logistics, and the price marks used to value the position. Nothing else on the wealth shelf ties as directly into the desk's structured-financing archetypes.

notes: METHOD AND CONFIDENCE. 45 web calls (28 searches, 17 fetches). Everything marked 'verified' comes from a bank's own product page, product booklet, information sheet, press release, a regulator's document, or named trade press, and the figure quoted is the one that document states. Items marked 'knowledge' are standard market practice that we could not tie to a public document in this pass - most PB yield-enhancement and financing terms are genuinely unpublished, which is the whole reason this gap exists in our 564-product catalogue. Three URLs would not render for us and should be re-pulled manually: the HKMA 2010 accumulator circular PDF, the Asian Private Banker 'Gold rush 2.0' piece (403), and Caproasia's write-up of the StanChart/AllianzGI fund (403). WHAT THE CATALOGUE IS MISSING, RANKED. (1) Lending values/advance rates on metal - 17-20 lombard_vs_metal records with no numbers anywhere; a single published or RM-sourced lending-value table would be the most valuable single addition. (2) The gold leg inside generic DCI/premium-account pages - several banks sell a gold DCI without saying so publicly (verified for HSBC Malaysia and Standard Chartered; likely at UOB, Maybank, BOC HK, BEA). (3) Payoff typing on the 60-66 structured_note records - we have names, not structures. (4) Accumulators/decumulators on gold - two knowledge-confidence records for a product that trade press says was one of the two biggest flow products in Asian private wealth in 2026. (5) Client gold repo and prepaid forwards - only Emirates NBD recorded. REGULATORY SENSITIVITIES. Hong Kong: the HKMA's March 2025 accumulator guidance effectively restricts accumulators to Professional Investors, mandates the highest risk rating, requires concentration assessment on FULL NOTIONAL (with a narrow FX-only flexibility framework), and requires explicit disclosure of knock-outs, multipliers, tenor and margin risk; the SFC/HKMA thematic review of non-exchange-traded product distribution (2024, ref 24EC21) is the companion suitability document. Anything we help a wealth business build in HK must survive both. Malaysia and Singapore: gold DCI/GCI is sold only to Sophisticated/Accredited Investors and is explicitly outside deposit insurance (CIMB states it is not PIDM-protected; Citi HK states GPI is not protected by any deposit protection scheme) - the marketing line 'deposit' is a compliance trap. Turkey: gold participation/FATSİ returns are part of a state gold-mobilisation scheme with a central-bank-funded uplift paid in TRY, so terms can change with policy. Shariah: AAOIFI Standard 57 requires real possession and rules out most option-based yield enhancement - do not assume a conventional structure ports. DESK POSITIONING. Six of these structures need nothing from the desk except volatility and forwards (DCI, puts, calls, notes, accumulators, options); three are the desk's own balance sheet (leasing/deposits, repo, prepay) and are where the margin and the metal actually are. The pitch to the wealth business should be sequenced accordingly: lead with the yield board (indicative DCI/put/collar yields quoted daily off our own volatility), and land the metal-deposit and repo capability as the differentiator, since most wealth platforms cannot source a lease rate or a liquidation bid internally. Also flag the mirror trade our desk has prioritised - the PM margin loan, where the client BORROWS against bullion or PM equity/ETF/streaming shares - which is the same client conversation approached from the financing side.
